```{r, VISUALIZATION}
library(ggplot2)

# bar plot 
ggplot(hotel_df,aes(x=reservation_status ,fill=hotel))+geom_bar(position = "dodge")+ labs(title = "Reservation Status",y="Count")

# scatter plot - Lead Time vs. Average Daily Rate
ggplot(hotel_df, aes(x = lead_time, y = adr, color = hotel)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(title = "Lead Time vs. Average Daily Rate",
       x = "Lead Time",
       y = "Average Daily Rate",
       color = "Hotel Type") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
# sample a subset of the dataset
sample_size<- 1000
hotel_data_sample<- hotel_df%>%sample_n(sample_size)
theme_set(theme_minimal())

# Create a histogram with distribution plot for lead time
ggplot(hotel_data_sample, aes(x = lead_time)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = ..density..), binwidth = 10, fill = "red", color = "green",
                 alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_density(color = "blue") +
  
  labs(title = "Hotel Booking Lead Time Distribution with Distribution Plot",
       x = "Lead Time (days)",
       y = "Density") +
  
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray", linetype = "dashed",size = 0.2),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
        legend.position = "none") +
  
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, max(hotel_data_sample$lead_time), by = 20))



# create a box plot to visualize outliers in "lead time " column

ggplot(hotel_df, aes(x = 1, y = lead_time)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "skyblue", color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Boxplot of Lead Time (Outlier Detection)",
       x = "",
       y = "Lead Time") +
  theme_minimal()

# Visualization Monthly Booking Trends
hotel_df %>%
  mutate(arrival_date_month = factor(arrival_date_month, levels = month.name)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = arrival_date_month, fill = hotel)) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge", stat = "count") +
  labs(title = "Monthly Booking Trends",
       x = "Month",
       y = "Number of Bookings",
       fill = "Hotel Type") +
  theme_minimal()

# Visualization Average Daily Rate (ADR) Distribution
ggplot(hotel_df, aes(x = adr, fill = hotel)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(title = "ADR Distribution by Hotel Type",
       x = "ADR",
       y = "Density",
       fill = "Hotel Type") +
  theme_minimal()


# Visualization  Market Segment Distribution
hotel_df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = market_segment, fill = hotel)) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge", stat = "count") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Bookings by Market Segment",
       x = "Market Segment",
       y = "Number of Bookings",
       fill = "Hotel Type") +
  theme_minimal()

```
```{r}
# Visualization: Most Preferred Hotel
 hotel_df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = hotel, fill = hotel)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "count", color = "white", size = 0.7) + 
  labs(title = "Distribution of Bookings by Hotel Type",
       x = "Hotel Type",
       y = "Number of Bookings",
       fill = "Hotel Type") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),  
        plot.title = element_text(size = 16, hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"), 
        legend.title = element_text(face = "italic"),  # Make legend title italic
        legend.position = "top",  # Position legend at the top
        panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "lightgray", linetype = "dashed")) 

# Visualization: Cancellation Patterns
hotel_df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = hotel, fill = as.factor(is_canceled))) +
  geom_bar(stat = "count", position = "stack") +
  labs(title = "Cancellation Patterns by Hotel Type",
       x = "Hotel Type",
       y = "Number of Bookings",
       fill = "Cancellation Status") +
  theme_minimal()


```

```{r}
# Visualization: Booking Distribution by Month
hotel_df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = arrival_date_month, fill = hotel)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "count", position = "stack") +
  labs(title = "Booking Distribution by Month",
       x = "Month",
       y = "Number of Bookings",
       fill = "Hotel Type") +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = function(x) formatC(as.numeric(x), width = 2, flag = "0"))

# Create a barplot for customer type distribution
ggplot(hotel_df, aes(x = customer_type, fill = customer_type)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Bookings by Customer Type",
       x = "Customer Type",
       y = "Number of Bookings") +
  theme_minimal()


```

```{r}

# Select numeric columns for correlation heatmap
numeric_columns <- hotel_df[, sapply(hotel_df, is.numeric)]

# Calculate the correlation matrix
correlation_matrix <- cor(numeric_columns)

# Convert correlation matrix to dataframe
correlation_df <- as.data.frame(as.table(correlation_matrix))

# Filter out diagonal values
correlation_df <- correlation_df[correlation_df$Var1 != correlation_df$Var2, ]

# Plot the heatmap
ggplot(data = correlation_df, aes(x = Var1, y = Var2, fill = Freq)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "blue", mid = "white", high = "red", midpoint = 0) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Correlation Heatmap of Numeric Columns",
       x = "Variables",
       y = "Variables",
       fill = "Correlation")


# Create a barplot for weekday vs. weekend bookings
hotel_df %>%
  mutate(booking_day_type = ifelse(stays_in_weekend_nights >0,"Weekend","Weekday"))%>%
  ggplot(aes(x = booking_day_type, fill = booking_day_type)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Bookings between Weekdays and Weekends",
       x = "Day Type",
       y = "Number of Bookings") +
  theme_minimal()
```
